questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: What does the abbreviation 'JKRLM' stand for?
options: Jammu & Kashmir Road and Land Management
Jammu & Kashmir Revenue and Land Ministry
questions.explanation: JKRLM stands for Jammu & Kashmir Rural Livelihood Mission, which works under the National Rural Livelihoods Mission (NRLM) to promote self-employment and livelihoods among rural poor. 'Road and Land Management' is incorrect as no such body exists with this abbreviation. 'Revenue and Land Ministry' is wrong because J&K does not have a ministry by that acronym. 'Regional Literacy Mission' is incorrect as the literacy mission operates under a different name.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about important dates related to J&K:

(i) The J&K Reorganisation Act, 2019 was passed by the Parliament on 5 August 2019.
(ii) The first Lok Sabha elections in J&K were held in 1967.
(iii) The Shimla Agreement was signed on 2 July 1972.
(iv) The J&K Constituent Assembly was dissolved in 1957.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Statement (i) is correct — the J&K Reorganisation Act was passed on 5 August 2019. Statement (iii) is correct — the Shimla Agreement between India and Pakistan was signed on 2 July 1972. Statement (iv) is correct — the J&K Constituent Assembly was dissolved on 26 January 1957 after adopting the state constitution. Statement (ii) is incorrect — the first Lok Sabha elections in J&K were held in 1957, not 1967.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The abbreviation 'LAHDC' refers to the Ladakh Autonomous Hill Development Council.
Reason (R): LAHDC was established in 1995 for Leh and 2003 for Kargil to provide autonomous governance to the hill areas of Ladakh.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Assertion (A) is correct — LAHDC stands for Ladakh Autonomous Hill Development Council. Reason (R) is also correct — LAHDC Leh was established in 1995 and LAHDC Kargil in 2003, specifically to provide autonomous self-governance to the hill areas. The Reason directly explains why the abbreviation LAHDC exists, making (R) the correct explanation of (A). Option B is wrong because the reason does explain the assertion. Option C is wrong because (R) is factually correct. Option D is wrong because (A) is factually correct.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Match the following abbreviations with their full forms:

Column I:
(a) JKSLSA
(b) JKPCC
(c) JKEDI
(d) JKRTC

Column II:
(i) J&K Entrepreneurship Development Institute
(ii) J&K State Legal Services Authority
(iii) J&K Road Transport Corporation
(iv) J&K Pollution Control Committee

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: JKSLSA stands for J&K State Legal Services Authority (a-ii). JKPCC stands for J&K Pollution Control Committee (b-iv). JKEDI stands for J&K Entrepreneurship Development Institute (c-i). JKRTC stands for J&K Road Transport Corporation (d-iii). Option B incorrectly pairs JKSLSA with pollution control. Option C incorrectly pairs JKPCC with the entrepreneurship institute. Option D incorrectly pairs JKSLSA with road transport.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Which of the following are correctly matched abbreviations related to J&K governance?

(i) JKSSB — Jammu & Kashmir Services Selection Board
(ii) JKPSC — Jammu & Kashmir Public Service Commission
(iii) JKBOSE — Jammu & Kashmir Board of Secondary Education
(iv) JKPDD — Jammu & Kashmir Power Development Department

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: Statement (i) is correct — JKSSB is Jammu & Kashmir Services Selection Board. Statement (ii) is correct — JKPSC is Jammu & Kashmir Public Service Commission. Statement (iv) is correct — JKPDD is Jammu & Kashmir Power Development Department. Statement (iii) is incorrect — JKBOSE stands for Jammu & Kashmir Board of School Education, not 'Board of Secondary Education'. The word is 'School' not 'Secondary'. Options B, C and D all include statement (iii) which is incorrect.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: In which year was the J&K State Constitution adopted by its Constituent Assembly?
questions.explanation: The J&K State Constitution was adopted on 17 November 1956 by the J&K Constituent Assembly and came into force on 26 January 1957. 1954 is incorrect — in that year the Presidential Order extended certain provisions of the Indian Constitution to J&K. 1957 is when the constitution came into force, not when it was adopted. 1952 is incorrect — that year saw the Delhi Agreement between Nehru and Sheikh Abdullah.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the J&K Official Languages Act, 2020:

(i) It recognizes Kashmiri, Dogri, Hindi, Urdu, and English as official languages.
(ii) It replaced the earlier J&K Official Languages Act, 1956.
(iii) Punjabi is not included among the official languages under this Act.
(iv) The Act was passed by the Parliament of India.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Statement (i) is correct — the Act recognizes Kashmiri, Dogri, Hindi, Urdu, and English as official languages of J&K UT. Statement (ii) is correct — it replaced the J&K Official Languages Act, 1956 which only recognized Urdu. Statement (iii) is correct — while Punjabi is spoken in some parts, it is not included in this Act. Statement (iv) is correct — since J&K became a UT, the Act was passed by the Parliament of India. All statements are factually accurate.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The Delhi Agreement of 1952 was signed between which two leaders?
options: Jawaharlal Nehru and Sheikh Mohammad Abdullah
Jawaharlal Nehru and Bakshi Ghulam Mohammad
Sardar Patel and Maharaja Hari Singh
Indira Gandhi and Sheikh Mohammad Abdullah
questions.correctAnswer: Jawaharlal Nehru and Sheikh Mohammad Abdullah
questions.explanation: The Delhi Agreement of 1952 was signed between Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru and J&K Premier Sheikh Mohammad Abdullah. It defined the scope of J&K's relationship with India. 'Nehru and Bakshi Ghulam Mohammad' is wrong as Bakshi became premier only after 1953. 'Sardar Patel and Maharaja Hari Singh' is wrong — Patel was involved in accession matters in 1947 but not this agreement. 'Indira Gandhi and Sheikh Abdullah' is wrong — their agreement (Kashmir Accord) came later in 1975.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The abbreviation 'SKIMS' stands for Sher-i-Kashmir Institute of Medical Sciences.
Reason (R): SKIMS was established in 1982 and is the premier medical institution of the Kashmir Valley located in Soura, Srinagar.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Assertion (A) is correct — SKIMS stands for Sher-i-Kashmir Institute of Medical Sciences. Reason (R) is also correct — SKIMS was established in 1982 and is located in Soura, Srinagar. However, the Reason does NOT explain the Assertion — the year of establishment and location explain the institution's importance, not what the abbreviation stands for. The abbreviation derives from the name of Sheikh Mohammad Abdullah (Sher-i-Kashmir). Option A is wrong because (R) doesn't explain (A). Option C is wrong because (R) is factually correct. Option D is wrong because (A) is factually correct.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The Instrument of Accession of J&K to India was signed by Maharaja Hari Singh on which date?
questions.explanation: Maharaja Hari Singh signed the Instrument of Accession on 26 October 1947. 22 October 1947 is the date of the tribal invasion into J&K. 24 October is not associated with any key event in this context. 27 October 1947 is when the Indian Army arrived in Srinagar to defend the state — this date is celebrated as Infantry Day.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: What does the abbreviation 'JKPCB' stand for?
options: Jammu & Kashmir Planning and Coordination Bureau
questions.explanation: JKPCB stands for Jammu & Kashmir Pollution Control Board, which is the regulatory body for environmental protection in J&K UT (now functioning as J&K Pollution Control Committee under the UT setup). 'Power Control Board' is incorrect — power is managed by JKPDD. 'Public Corporations Bureau' does not exist. 'Planning and Coordination Bureau' is fabricated and not a real institution.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the Kashmir Accord of 1975:

(i) It was signed between Indira Gandhi and Sheikh Mohammad Abdullah.
(ii) It restored Sheikh Abdullah as the Chief Minister of J&K.
(iii) It formally revoked Article 370 of the Constitution.
(iv) It accepted the relationship of J&K with India as governed by Article 370.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Statement (i) is correct — the accord was between PM Indira Gandhi and Sheikh Abdullah. Statement (ii) is correct — Sheikh Abdullah became CM again in 1975 after the accord. Statement (iv) is correct — the accord accepted that J&K's relationship with India would continue under Article 370. Statement (iii) is incorrect — the accord did NOT revoke Article 370; in fact it reaffirmed its applicability. Article 370 was abrogated much later in 2019.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Match the following important dates with events in J&K history:

Column I:
(a) 5 August 2019
(b) 26 January 1957
(c) 13 November 1947
(d) 17 November 1956

Column II:
(i) J&K State Constitution adopted
(ii) Abrogation of Article 370
(iii) Liberation of Baramulla from tribal raiders
(iv) J&K Constitution came into force

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: 5 August 2019 is when Article 370 was abrogated (a-ii). 26 January 1957 is when the J&K Constitution came into force (b-iv). 13 November 1947 marks the liberation of Baramulla from tribal raiders by the Indian Army (c-iii). 17 November 1956 is when the J&K State Constitution was adopted by the Constituent Assembly (d-i). Option B incorrectly pairs the abrogation date with the constitution coming into force. Option C swaps the Baramulla liberation with the constitution event. Option D misassigns all major dates.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Which of the following abbreviations are associated with financial institutions in J&K?

(i) J&K Bank
(ii) J&K Grameen Bank
(iii) JKIDFC
(iv) JKBOSE

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: J&K Bank is the premier banking institution (i — correct). J&K Grameen Bank is a regional rural bank for credit in rural areas (ii — correct). JKIDFC is the J&K Infrastructure Development Finance Corporation, a financial institution (iii — correct). JKBOSE is the J&K Board of School Education, which is an educational body, not a financial institution (iv — incorrect). Options B, C and D all include JKBOSE which is not a financial institution.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The ceasefire between India and Pakistan in J&K came into effect on which date?
questions.explanation: The UN-mandated ceasefire between India and Pakistan came into effect on 1 January 1949. 27 July 1949 is incorrect — this date is associated with the Karachi Agreement that established the ceasefire line. 5 January 1949 is incorrect — on this date the UN Security Council adopted a resolution but the ceasefire had already taken effect. 15 August 1948 has no significance in this context.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the Jammu & Kashmir Bank:

(i) It was founded in 1938.
(ii) Its headquarters are in Srinagar.
(iii) It was designated as a public sector bank after 2019 reorganization.
(iv) It functions as a scheduled commercial bank.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Statement (i) is correct — J&K Bank was established on 1 October 1938. Statement (ii) is correct — its headquarters are in Srinagar. Statement (iv) is correct — it is a scheduled commercial bank. Statement (iii) is incorrect — J&K Bank remains a listed entity (the UT government holds majority shares) but it is classified differently; it was not designated as a 'public sector bank' in the traditional PSB sense under RBI norms.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: What does the abbreviation 'SKUAST' stand for?
options: Sher-e-Kashmir University of Agricultural Sciences and Technology
State of Kashmir University for Applied Science and Technology
Shri Krishna University of Arts, Science and Technology
Sher-e-Kashmir University of Advanced Studies and Teaching
questions.correctAnswer: Sher-e-Kashmir University of Agricultural Sciences and Technology
questions.explanation: SKUAST stands for Sher-e-Kashmir University of Agricultural Sciences and Technology, with two campuses — SKUAST-K in Shalimar (Kashmir) and SKUAST-J in Chatha (Jammu). 'State of Kashmir University for Applied Science and Technology' is fabricated. 'Shri Krishna University' is invented. 'University of Advanced Studies and Teaching' is also not a real institution.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): 26 October is observed as 'Accession Day' in Jammu & Kashmir.
Reason (R): On 26 October 1947, the Indian Army landed in Srinagar to defend the state against tribal invaders.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: (A) is correct but (R) is not correct
questions.explanation: Assertion (A) is correct — 26 October is observed as Accession Day because Maharaja Hari Singh signed the Instrument of Accession on this date. Reason (R) is factually incorrect — the Indian Army landed in Srinagar on 27 October 1947 (the day after accession was signed), not on 26 October. The accession was signed on 26th and the troops arrived on the morning of 27th. Option A is wrong because (R) has an incorrect date. Option B is wrong because (R) is not correct. Option D is wrong because (A) is correct.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: Fill in the blank: The abbreviation 'JKERA' stands for Jammu & Kashmir __________ Regulatory Authority.
questions.explanation: JKERA stands for Jammu & Kashmir Electricity Regulatory Authority, which regulates the generation, supply, and tariff of electricity in the UT. 'Education' is incorrect — the education regulator has a different name. 'Environment' is wrong — environmental regulation falls under JKPCB/JKPCC. 'Employment' is incorrect — no such regulatory authority exists with this acronym.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The Quit Kashmir Movement was launched by Sheikh Mohammad Abdullah in which year?
questions.explanation: The Quit Kashmir Movement was launched by Sheikh Mohammad Abdullah in 1946, demanding the end of Dogra rule. 1944 is incorrect — the National Conference was formed in that year (renamed from Muslim Conference). 1947 is the year of the tribal invasion and accession, not the Quit Kashmir movement. 1948 is when UN resolutions on J&K were passed.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Match the following abbreviations with their associated sectors:

Column I:
(a) JKHPMC
(b) JKSFDC
(c) JKPDD
(d) JKTDC

Column II:
(i) Tourism
(ii) Horticulture
(iii) Power/Electricity
(iv) Forest

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: JKHPMC is J&K Horticultural Produce Marketing Corporation — related to horticulture (a-ii). JKSFDC is J&K State Forest Development Corporation — related to forests (b-iv). JKPDD is J&K Power Development Department — related to power/electricity (c-iii). JKTDC is J&K Tourism Development Corporation — related to tourism (d-i). Option B swaps horticulture with forests and misassigns power. Option C incorrectly pairs JKSFDC with power. Option D incorrectly pairs JKHPMC with tourism.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the Dogra period in J&K:

(i) Maharaja Gulab Singh was the first Dogra ruler of J&K from 1846.
(ii) Maharaja Hari Singh was the last ruling Dogra monarch.
(iii) The Dogra dynasty ruled J&K for approximately 100 years.
(iv) Maharaja Pratap Singh introduced the Praja Sabha in 1922.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Statement (i) is correct — Gulab Singh became ruler in 1846 via the Treaty of Amritsar. Statement (ii) is correct — Hari Singh was the last ruling Dogra monarch who signed the Instrument of Accession in 1947. Statement (iii) is correct — from 1846 to 1947, roughly 101 years. Statement (iv) is correct — Maharaja Pratap Singh introduced the Praja Sabha (People's Assembly) in 1922 as a representative body. All four statements are factually accurate.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The J&K National Conference was originally founded as the 'Muslim Conference' in which year?
questions.explanation: The All Jammu & Kashmir Muslim Conference was founded on 16 October 1932 by Sheikh Mohammad Abdullah. It was later renamed to National Conference in 1939 to make it a secular organization. 1930 is incorrect — it is associated with civil rights movements but not the founding of the party. 1934 and 1936 are incorrect dates.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
The following data shows the number of government institutions established in J&K during different decades:

| Decade | Universities | Engineering Colleges | Medical Colleges |
|--------|-------------|---------------------|------------------|
| 1950s–1960s | 2 | 1 | 1 |
| 1970s–1980s | 1 | 2 | 1 |
| 1990s–2000s | 3 | 4 | 2 |
| 2010s–2020s | 5 | 6 | 4 |

In which period was the total number of institutions established the highest?
questions.explanation: 2010s–2020s: 5 + 6 + 4 = 15 institutions (highest). 1990s–2000s: 3 + 4 + 2 = 9 institutions. 1970s–1980s: 1 + 2 + 1 = 4 institutions. 1950s–1960s: 2 + 1 + 1 = 4 institutions. The 2010s–2020s period saw the maximum institutional growth due to centrally-funded projects like IIT Jammu, AIIMS, and new medical/engineering colleges.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: What does the abbreviation 'SMVDU' stand for in J&K?
options: State Medical and Veterinary Department Unit
Srinagar Municipal and Village Development Union
questions.explanation: SMVDU stands for Shri Mata Vaishno Devi University, located in Katra, Reasi district. It was established in 1999 by an Act of the J&K State Legislature. 'State Medical and Veterinary Department Unit' is fabricated. 'Sher-e-Kashmir Memorial Vocational Development Unit' is not a real institution. 'Srinagar Municipal and Village Development Union' does not exist.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Which of the following events occurred in J&K in the year 1989?

(i) Beginning of armed insurgency in the Kashmir Valley
(ii) Kidnapping of Rubiya Sayeed
(iii) Mass exodus of Kashmiri Pandits from the Valley
(iv) Imposition of Governor's rule in the state

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: Statement (i) is correct — 1989 marks the beginning of armed insurgency in the Kashmir Valley. Statement (ii) is correct — Rubiya Sayeed (daughter of then Home Minister Mufti Mohammad Sayeed) was kidnapped in December 1989. Statement (iii) is incorrect — the mass exodus of Kashmiri Pandits occurred in January 1990, not 1989. Statement (iv) is incorrect — Governor's rule was imposed in January 1990 after the government fell. Options B, C, and D all include events that happened in 1990.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The Muslim Conference was renamed as 'National Conference' in which year?
questions.explanation: The All Jammu & Kashmir Muslim Conference was renamed as National Conference on 11 June 1939 by Sheikh Mohammad Abdullah to make it a secular political party. 1937 is incorrect — it is associated with provincial elections in British India. 1938 is incorrect — that year the J&K Bank was established. 1941 is incorrect — it was an unremarkable year for this renaming event.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
The following data shows the timeline of key constitutional/administrative changes in J&K:

| Year | Event | Days since previous event |
|------|-------|---------------------------|
| 1947 | Accession | — |
| 1950 | Presidential Order (C.O. 10) | ~1,092 |
| 1952 | Delhi Agreement | ~730 |
| 1954 | Presidential Order (C.O. 48) | ~730 |

What is the approximate total number of days between the Accession and the Presidential Order of 1954?
questions.explanation: Adding the intervals: 1,092 + 730 + 730 = 2,552 days from Accession (1947) to the Presidential Order of 1954. Option A (2,192) results from adding only the first two intervals. Option C (2,922) adds an extra 370 days erroneously. Option D (1,822) represents only the first two intervals incorrectly computed.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: What does the abbreviation 'JKSAC' stand for?
questions.explanation: JKSAC stands for Jammu & Kashmir State Accountability Commission, established to check corruption and ensure accountability of public servants. 'State Advisory Council' is incorrect — while such advisory councils exist, JKSAC specifically refers to the accountability body. 'Sports Activities Council' is fabricated. 'Social Audit Committee' does not carry this abbreviation.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: In which year did Maharaja Hari Singh introduce the 'Hereditary State Subject' definition (State Subject Rule) in J&K?
questions.explanation: Maharaja Hari Singh introduced the Hereditary State Subject definition (also known as the State Subject Rule) in 1927 to define who was a permanent resident of J&K. 1925 is incorrect — that year Hari Singh ascended the throne but did not introduce this rule immediately. 1929 is incorrect — it is an unrelated year in this context. 1932 is incorrect — that year saw the founding of the Muslim Conference.
